threads.body: [Build] A named suite declared with `register<JvmTestSuite>("integrationTest") { executions { ... } }` can remain unrealized when running `check`: this lazy callback does not realize it, and its `check` dependencies are only added inside the suite's configuration. Without another reference that realizes the suite, `check` silently skips both its default execution and variants. The named-suite test hides this by calling `.get()` first. Eagerly configure suite registrations here, and add a regression that resolves `check` dependencies without first realizing the named suite or its tasks.

replies.body:
No code change.

Not reproducible on the frozen repository's pinned Gradle 9.8.1. TestSuiteExecutionsPlugin applies jvm-test-suite before attaching its configureEach callback (TestSuiteExecutions.kt:18-21). Gradle 9.8.1 JvmTestSuitePlugin.apply already installs testing.suites.withType(JvmTestSuite).all(...), and its callback also installs targets.all(...). Consequently register<JvmTestSuite>("integrationTest") executes the suite configuration without an explicit provider.get(), and the existing code adds both default and variant tasks to check (TestSuiteExecutions.kt:56-73). An investigation-only ProjectBuilder regression resolved check dependencies without first realizing the named suite or any Test tasks and passed unchanged; it observed test, integrationTest, and integrationTestExperimental. A separate evaluated Kotlin DSL build using the exact register<JvmTestSuite> form also included both named-suite tasks in check --dry-run, with an assertion that no Test task was realized during configuration. The existing seven convention tests passed after removing the investigation-only test. Changing configureEach to all would not fix a supported failure on this frozen build.
